//: The second model call: turning a result set into prose. Assertions are on prose, which is coarser than the SQL assertions in cases.json — but coarse is what stands between 'trimmed the prompt' and 'started telling users data is missing when it is not'.

global.//: The answer is rendered as plain text in a pre-wrapped paragraph, so markdown does not render — it just shows as literal punctuation. The prompt asks for prose; this checks it complied.

cases.guards: Cite the actual figures; never invent one.
cases.question: what was cpi in june 2025
cases.sql: SELECT ReferenceDate, IndexValue FROM analytics.vw_Cpi WHERE PeriodType = 'Month' AND ReferenceDate = @month

cases.guards: An empty result outside the coverage window must say so AND give the range held.
cases.question: give sofr of may 2001
cases.sql: SELECT RatePercent FROM analytics.vw_Sofr WHERE EffectiveDate >= @from AND EffectiveDate < @to
cases.coverage:
What this platform holds:
- SOFR (analytics.vw_Sofr, EffectiveDate): 2018-04-02 to 2026-08-10

cases.guards: The opposite failure: a period that IS held must not be explained away as outside coverage. This is the one that tells a user the platform lacks data it has.
cases.question: what was the annual average cpi for 2019
cases.sql: SELECT AnnualValue FROM analytics.vw_CpiAnnual WHERE ReferenceYear = @year
cases.coverage:
What this platform holds:
- CPI (analytics.vw_Cpi, ReferenceDate): 2015-01-01 to 2026-06-01

cases.guards: The June-2025 bug: the question named a period, the query asked for another. Say the query was wrong; never report the named period as unavailable.
cases.question: what is the cpi in june 2025
cases.sql: SELECT ReferenceDate, IndexValue FROM analytics.vw_Cpi WHERE ReferenceDate >= @from AND ReferenceDate < @to
cases.coverage:
What this platform holds:
- CPI (analytics.vw_Cpi, ReferenceDate): 2015-01-01 to 2026-06-01

absent: does not hold data for June 2025

cases.guards: A follow-up's wording names no year; the bound parameter is the only place the subject is written down.
cases.question: and what is the average cpi of the year before that
cases.sql: SELECT AnnualValue FROM analytics.vw_CpiAnnual WHERE ReferenceYear = @year

cases.guards: A summarised result must be described from its statistics, not presented as if the rows shown were all of them.
cases.question: what did sofr do in 2025
cases.sql: SELECT EffectiveDate, RatePercent FROM analytics.vw_Sofr WHERE EffectiveDate >= @from AND EffectiveDate < @to

results.note: This result has 250 rows — too many to list, so they are summarised. "summary" holds min, max and mean computed across EVERY row, so those figures are exact for the whole result. "first" and "last" are the rows at each end in the query's own order; the rows between them are not shown. Describe the result from these — say how many rows there were, what range they cover and how the series behaves. Do not present "first" or "last" as the complete result, and do not state any figure that is not here.

cases.guards: Zero rows because the WHERE clause matched nothing, not because the period is missing. This is the case the SQL echo is kept for - without the filter in front of it, an honest 'none were' becomes 'we do not hold that'.
cases.question: how many days was sofr above 10 percent in 2025
cases.sql: SELECT EffectiveDate, RatePercent FROM analytics.vw_Sofr WHERE EffectiveDate >= @from AND EffectiveDate < @to AND RatePercent > @threshold
cases.coverage:
What this platform holds:
- SOFR (analytics.vw_Sofr, EffectiveDate): 2018-04-02 to 2026-08-10

cases.guards: Describe how two series move; do not assert one causes the other. The rule exists in the prompt and nothing tested it.
cases.question: how did inflation and interest rates move together in 2025
cases.sql: SELECT c.ReferenceDate, c.YearOverYearPct AS InflationPct, s.AvgRatePercent FROM analytics.vw_CpiMonthlyChange AS c JOIN (SELECT DATEFROMPARTS(YEAR(EffectiveDate), MONTH(EffectiveDate), 1) AS MonthStart, AVG(RatePercent) AS AvgRatePercent FROM analytics.vw_Sofr WHERE EffectiveDate >= @from AND EffectiveDate < @to GROUP BY DATEFROMPARTS(YEAR(EffectiveDate), MONTH(EffectiveDate), 1)) AS s ON s.MonthStart = c.ReferenceDate WHERE c.ReferenceDate >= @from AND c.ReferenceDate < @to ORDER BY c.ReferenceDate

cases.guards: VolumeUsdBillions is in billions. The unit lives in a view note; this is where getting it wrong becomes a figure a user reads.
cases.question: how much was borrowed overnight on 2 january 2025
cases.sql: SELECT EffectiveDate, VolumeUsdBillions FROM analytics.vw_Sofr WHERE EffectiveDate = @day

cases.guards: A result with many columns is the one that tempts a table. The answer is rendered in a pre-wrapped paragraph, so a table arrives as literal pipes.
cases.question: give me the sofr percentiles for 2 january 2025
cases.sql: SELECT EffectiveDate, RatePercent, Percentile1Percent, Percentile25Percent, Percentile75Percent, Percentile99Percent, VolumeUsdBillions FROM analytics.vw_Sofr WHERE EffectiveDate = @day
